definition: Every chart belongs to one of two sects, day or night, set by whether the Sun is above or below the horizon. Each planet has its own sect affiliation, and a planet operates more comfortably when its sect matches the chart's.

chartSect.diurnal: Sun above the horizon (day chart). The Sun is the sect light.
chartSect.nocturnal: Sun below the horizon (night chart). The Moon is the sect light.

mercuryRule: Mercury is common: diurnal when it rises before the Sun (oriental), nocturnal when it sets after the Sun (occidental).
inSect: A planet in sect operates more constructively and is better able to deliver its significations.
outOfSect: A planet out of sect is less stable. The out-of-sect malefic is the harsher of the two: Saturn is most difficult in a night chart, Mars most difficult in a day chart.
paradox: The malefics are placed in the sect opposite their nature so they can be tempered: cold, heavy Saturn is warmed by the day sect; hot, volatile Mars is cooled by the night sect.
testimony: Benefics regarding (aspecting) a malefic can moderate or restrain it; a malefic overcome by Jupiter or Venus does less damage.
summary: Sect distinguishes day charts from night charts and determines which benefic or malefic is most constructive or difficult.
